main_text.l: Nos manet Oceanus circumvagus; arva, beata
main_text.p: And that the pole antarctic was seen by them there, as the arctic, or north pole is by us here, according to that of Virgil in his Georgics :
main_text.l: Hic vertex nobis semper sublimis : at illum
Sub pedibus Styx atra videt, manesque profundi.
main_text.p: Fifthly, as they held that Hades was for situation placed from the centre of the earth downward ; so betwixt the beginning and the lowest part thereof they imagined as great a space to be interjected, as there is betwixt heaven and earth. So saith Apollodorus of Tartarus, the dungeon of torment: "Thiss is a dark place in Hades, having as great a distance from the earth, as the earth from the heaven." And Hesiod in his Theogonia (agreeably to that which before we heard from Homer)
main_text.l: Τόσσον ἐνερθ' ὑπὸ γῆς ὅσον οὐρανὸς ἐστ' ἀπὸ γαίης·
Ἴσον γάρ' τ' ἀπὸ γῆς ἐς τάρταρον ἠερόεντα.
main_text.p: "It is as far beneath the earth, as heaven is from the earth: for thus equal is the distance from the earth unto dark Tartarus." Whereunto that of Virgil may be added, in the sixth of the Æneids:
main_text.l: Bis patet in præceps tantum tenditque sub umbras,
Quantus ad æthereum cœli suspectus Olympum.
——— then Tartarus itself, that sink-hole steep
Two times as low descends, two times as headlong downright deep
main_text.p: * Τόπος δὲ οὗτος ἱρεβώδης ἐστὶν ἐν ᾅδου, τοσοῦτον ἀπὸ γῆς ἔχων διάστημα, ὅσον ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ γῆ. Apollodor. bibliothec. lib. 1.
¹ Τὸ δὲ βάθος τὸ πολλὸν τοῦ ἡέρος, τάρταρος καλέεται. Lucian. περὶ ἀστρολογίας.
